subject: How can I obtaine predictions for a testing dataset

messages.author: e572b218e461758a
messages.subject: How can I obtaine predictions for a testing dataset
parts:
Dear list,

I split my dataset in training data set and testing dataset.

I´d like to obtaine predictions for the testing dataset after fitting the model ussing the training dataset.

How can I do this? 

Many thanks in advance 

Here´s a toy example:

y=c(75.2,145.4,99.6,168.6,152.2,173.1,152.1,169.7,130.1,117.1,124.1,119.4,134.6,90.7,
    98.3,89.2,128.4,145.6,130.7,69.8,246,166.7,95.8,135.9,98.1,97.1,202.1,75.3,100.7,
    100.4,153.5,194.6)
E=c(80.7,169.8,123.2,139.5,169.1,107.2,179.8,160.4,147.5,
    116.8,102.8,91.8,119.6,114.8,131.1,136.1,116.6,98.5,
    88.8,79.8,144.9,134.7,98.9,118.6,130.6,96.1,127.1,97.7,
    88.5,121.4,156.8,114)
x1=c(0.87,-0.96,-0.84,0.13,-1.19,0.35,-0.84,-0.18,-0.39,0.74,
     1.93,0.24,0.59,-1.15,-0.8,-0.59,-0.12,1.43,-0.04,-1.24,1,
     0.53,-0.75,1.36,-0.93,-1.24,1.68,-1.04,2.38,0.03,-0.2,0.14)
x2=c(-1.02,-0.33,-1.43,-0.1,-0.98,1.77,-0.73,-0.2,-0.96,-0.58,
     0.36,1.48,0.46,-0.93,-1.62,-0.96,-0.48,0.81,2.41,-0.4,
     0.71,-0.05,-0.33,-0.47,-0.92,0.06,0.22,-0.73,0.1,-0.59,
     0.7,2.28)
Data<-as.data.frame(cbind(y=y, E=E, x1=x1, x2=x2))
set.seed(1974); ind <- sample(2, nrow(Data), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.8, 0.2))
trainData <- Data[ind==1,]
testData <- Data[ind==2,]
formula = Biom ~ 1 +  Slope+TWI+ctan
formula <- y ~ 1 + E + x1 + x2
result<- inla(formula,family="lognormal",data=trainData,
              control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
              control.compute=list(config = TRUE,cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE, waic = TRUE))

exp(result$summary.fitted.values[1:5])

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How can I obtaine predictions for a testing dataset
parts: Instead of actually splitting it, just assign NA for 'y':

On 10/04/2017 05:57 AM, Mike wrote:
> set.seed(1974); ind <- sample(2, nrow(Data), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.8,
> 0.2))

Data$y[id==2] <- NA

and use it with link=1 in:

result<- inla(formula,family="lognormal",data=Data,
              control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1),
